hook: Four hundred and seventy wins in a row. Ten years without losing once.
story: Her name is Esther Vergeer. A nine-hour spinal operation at age eight left her legs paralyzed; she found tennis in rehab. In January 2003, a player named Daniela di Toro beat her in Sydney. No one ever did it again. Over the next ten years she collected seven Paralympic golds, forty-three Grand Slam titles, and six hundred and sixty-eight straight weeks at world number one.
number: Four hundred and fifty-two of those four hundred and seventy wins never even reached a deciding set. The longest streak anyone has managed in standing tennis is seventy-four. And in ten years of matches, her opponents earned exactly one match point. One. The Beijing Paralympic final, 2008. She saved it, took the gold, and no one ever got that close again.
closer: She retired at thirty-one, still world number one. Nobody ever ended the streak.

And in ten years of matches, her opponents earned exactly one match point. One. The Beijing Paralympic final, 2008. She saved it, took the gold, and no one ever got that close again.
